notes: New apps automatically publish saved changes after their first successful publish. You can turn automatic publishing off or on from your app’s management page.
New apps that require Cedarville sign-in now have a dedicated sign-in page. Existing apps show guidance for adding one.
If your first publish fails, you can now open app details to adjust settings or delete the app before trying again.
Administrators can now see when each user last signed in.
App names must now be unique, helping you avoid confusing one app with another.
After your existing app is prepared, publishing setup now completes automatically so you can move straight to publishing.
When adding an existing app, you can choose to add a database and require Cedarville sign-in.
Codex guidance for existing apps now reuses your current project folder.
Codex now gives clearer help connecting to your app’s code and resolving sign-in problems.
Browser tabs now show clearer page titles and the CU Launch icon.
Activity dates shown to administrators now default to Eastern time.
The shared-app area is now called Cedarville Apps, with clearer guidance about sharing your app.
Fixed a problem that could interrupt publishing while an app was still making progress.
Setup guidance now explains how Mac users get Git through Cedarville and when to contact IT for help.
Edit several app settings together and save them in one step. You can undo a deletion or discard unsaved changes.
Publishing now runs in the background, with better tools for administrators to recover interrupted attempts.
When an existing app needs changes before it can be published, setup now explains the problem and guides you back to Codex for repairs.
Creating or adding an app now follows a guided setup with clearer progress and next steps.
The home page has a refreshed look, and My Apps makes it easier to find and manage your work.
Choosing an app that is already on GitHub now takes you directly to the right setup screen.
A single Launch Your App button now helps you choose the right starting point.
Find Settings and Log Out together in the menu under your name.
The Codex connection now uses the CU Launch name consistently, making it easier to identify the right portal.
Collaborators now see their own code-access status, so one person’s invitation or error is not shown to someone else.
Improved publishing support for Python apps so required software is installed automatically during publishing.
When creating an app, you can choose whether it is openly public or requires Cedarville sign-in.
Setup uses simpler language to explain what happens next.
Clearer repair guidance helps Codex prepare existing apps for publishing.
